title: Institutional and Procedural Frameworks
summary: This thread covers the establishment and modification of specific institutional bodies and procedural rules, such as the AEO committee and freight forwarder licensing, which are distinct from the routine amendment of tax notifications.

evolution.institutional_structure: Formalization of administrative committees under the new Customs Act 2023.

timeline.change: Formal establishment of the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) committee.

Authorized Economic Operator: The Authorized Economic Operator committee is established to oversee activities, evaluate applications for recognition, and provide recommendations on granting, rejecting, or conditionally approving status based on risk assessment and intelligence.
The committee is responsible for making decisions regarding the upgrading or downgrading of status, the cancellation of recognition, and the overall governance of program activities.

The committee shall provide necessary policy advice, consult with stakeholders and experts, recommend amendments to existing laws, and submit an annual report on program activities to the head of the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue acts as the overarching authority, with a designated member serving as the chairperson of the Authorized Economic Operator committee.
The committee is mandated to submit its annual progress report and recommendations for legal or regulatory changes to the National Board of Revenue.
World Customs Organization: The committee is authorized to co-opt subject matter experts, including those recognized or accredited by the World Customs Organization, to assist in its functions.
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: The committee is composed of various officials from the National Board of Revenue, customs intelligence, risk management, and valuation units, with the authority to hold monthly meetings chaired by a designated board member.
The chairperson is responsible for determining meeting procedures and ensuring that the committee meets at least once a month to ensure the smooth conduct of operational tasks.

Authorized Economic Operator: head of the National Board of Revenue

এস.আর.ও. নং ২৩১-আইন/২০২৪/৫৩/কাস্টমস।— সরকার, কাস্টমস আইন, ২০২৩ (২০২৩ সনের ৫৭ নং আইন) এর ধারা ২৬৩, ধারা ১১ ও ১২ এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সহিত পরামর্শক্রমে, ওয়্যারহাউস লাইসেন্সিং বিধিমালা, ২০২৪ এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা:-

উপরিউক্ত বিধিমালার-

Customs Act 2023: The Government is empowered under Section 263, read with Sections 11 and 12, to issue regulations and amendments regarding customs procedures.
This Act provides the foundational authority for the government to act in consultation with the National Board of Revenue to amend warehouse licensing rules.
National Board of Revenue: The government is required to consult with the National Board of Revenue before exercising its legal authority to amend the warehouse licensing rules.
Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024: These rules are subject to further amendment by the government under the powers granted by the Customs Act 2023.

এস,আর,ও নং- ১৩৯-আইন/২০১৪/২৫০৩/কাস্টমস ।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 207 ও section 219 এবং THIRD SCHEDULE এর Item 21 এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড, ফ্রেইট ফরওয়ার্ডার্স (লাইসেন্সিং ও কার্য-পরিচালনা) বিধিমালা, ২০০৮ এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা :-

উপরি-উক্ত বিধিমালা-

Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the statutory authority under its sections and schedules for the National Board of Revenue to issue or amend regulations relating to customs licensing and operational procedures.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered by the Customs Act to amend and formulate specific rules governing the licensing and operations of freight forwarders.
Freight Forwarders (Licensing and Operat: These rules are subject to further amendment by the National Board of Revenue under the powers granted by the Customs Act.
Third Schedule: The Third Schedule is referenced alongside specific sections of the Customs Act as the legal basis for the National Board of Revenue to issue these amendments.
